info.bio:
Barenaked Ladies (o BNL abreviado) es un grupo Canadiense de rock alternativo formado por Kevin Hearn, Ed Robertson, Steven Page, Tyler Stewart, y Jim Creeggan. La banda se formó en 1988 en Scarborough, Ontario, un suburbio de Toronto. BNL tiene una gran reputación como banda en directo y son especialmente conocidos por improvisar canciones cómicas durante sus actuaciones


La primera grabación del grupo, Buck Naked, publicada en 1989, se grabó en sótanos y habitaciones, y en ella solo participaron Steve y Ed.

scenes.name: Renacimiento pop, Elephant 6 y lounge-pop
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: En la primera mitad de los noventa el pop supera ampliamente a la música experimental: la revancha de la melodía tras un cuarto de siglo de sonidos progresivos. La vía más rentable sigue el pop barroco de los últimos Beach Boys, Van Dyke Parks, Big Star y XTC: Jellyfish (Bellybutton), Imperial Teen, Velvet Crush, Material Issue, Eggs, Fountains Of Wayne, Ben Folds Five, Chainsaw Kittens, Barenaked Ladies. El colectivo «Elephant 6» de Georgia y Luisiana es la escuela pop más influyente de la década: Apples In Stereo, Olivia Tremor Control, Neutral Milk Hotel (In The Aeroplane Over The Sea), Elf Power, Of Montreal; y sus herederos Ladybug Transistor y Photon Band. El folk-pop a lo Tom Petty y R.E.M.; el «lounge-pop» (Combustible Edison, Zumpano, Ivy, Cardigans, Squirrel Nut Zippers); el teen-pop (Hanson, Britney Spears, Backstreet Boys).

podcast.title: "The Yellow Tape" Platinum Certification (1991)
podcast.body: In 1991, the Barenaked Ladies' independently released cassette, "The Yellow Tape," sold nearly 100,000 copies, a remarkable achievement for an unsigned Canadian band during an era dominated by major labels. This success made it the first-ever indie release to be certified platinum in Canadian music history. "That was the first ever indie release to be certified platinum in the history of Canadian music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "The Yellow Tape" Platinum Certification (1991)
podcast.body: "The Yellow Tape" cassette, self-released by the Barenaked Ladies in 1991, became the first independent music release in the history of Canadian music to be certified platinum, selling nearly 100,000 copies. "That was the first ever indie release to be certified platinum in the history of Canadian music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Rise in 1991
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies began their rise in 1991, becoming part of a new crop of Canadian artists gaining prominence. Their emergence signaled the expansion of the "Can Rock explosion" beyond its initial wave. "1991, so the beginning of the rise of the Barodicad Ladies, Spirit of the West, Sarah McLaughlin, Crash Vegas, Crash Test Dummies, and Grapes of Wrath."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Roots of the 90s CanRock Explosion

podcast.title: The Yellow Tape (1991)
podcast.body: Despite persistent rejections from record labels, the band released a cassette called "The Yellow Tape" in 1991, primarily to meet demand from their loyal cult following. It sold nearly 100,000 copies directly from their performances, becoming the first indie release in Canadian music history to be certified platinum, eventually leading to a major label deal. "In 1991 they released a cassette called The Yellow Tape because, well it was yellow. And the whole idea was to satisfy demands from fans. They sold so many off the stage that it ended up becoming a legitimate commercial release selling nearly 100,000 copies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: 1992 Toronto Concert Ban – Name Deemed Objectifying Despite Band's Explanation
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies were banned from performing at a Toronto concert in 1992 because city officials considered their name objectifying toward women. The band explained that the name was intended as harmless "childlike language," but the ban was upheld regardless. "The band explained the name was 'childlike language,' but the ban was maintained."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Continued Rise in 1992
podcast.body: The band continued to gain momentum in 1992, further establishing their presence in the thriving Canadian music scene. "More Hip, More Barodicad Ladies."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Bananas and Scotch
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies used to ask for 20 pounds of bananas, along with one good bottle of single malt scotch, in their rider. "The bear naked ladies used to ask for 20 pounds of bananas for some reason, along with one good bottle of single malt scotch."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Backstage Rider – Dietary Open-Mindedness with Exclusions
podcast.body: The band and crew described themselves as "very open-minded yet health conscious about their diets," welcoming diverse meal ideas like Turkey dinner, Indian, Japanese, Meatloaf, or Ham and Scalloped potatoes. However, they explicitly requested not to be offered "chicken breast or vegetarian lasagna again," suggesting these items had become overused. "So please don't offer chicken breast or vegetarian lasagna again."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Career Comeback
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies were once written off, but they managed to roar back to life in their career. "The barren-naked ladies were once written off before roaring back to life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall and Rise of Blink 182 Part 2

podcast.title: Early Busking and Performance Art Origins
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies began their career in Toronto as eccentric buskers, almost resembling performance artists. Their early shows were distinctly geeky and nerdy, characterized by the unique humor channeled by founding members Ed Robertson and Steven Page. "Toronto's bare naked ladies were launching their career as weird buskers. They were almost performance artists of some sort."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Early Busking and Performance Art Origins
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies began their career as unusual buskers in Toronto, often described as performance artists due to their geeky and nerdy style. "Toronto's bare naked ladies were launching their career as weird buskers. They were almost performance artists of some sort."

podcast.title: Early Career Success
podcast.body: The Barenaked Ladies commenced their fruitful multi-decade career in the very late 1980s or early 1990s, becoming one of the "stars" who emerged during the Canadian music boom. They were recognized for their success alongside other prominent Canadian acts. "the bear naked ladies...had fruitful multi-decade careers that began in either the very late 1980s or the early 1990s."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: Lost CanRock Bands of the '90s: Part 1

podcast.title: Early Independent Success
podcast.body: Starting as "goofy buskers," Barenaked Ladies independently released a cassette that sold 80,000 copies, creating such high demand that major chain stores like Sam the Record Man were compelled to stock it. "The bear naked ladies started out as a bunch of goofy buskers. But then they ended up selling 80,000 copies of an independently released cassette."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Fan Tradition of Throwing Craft Dinner
podcast.body: To this day, fans of the Barenaked Ladies continue a tradition of throwing boxes of Kraft Dinner (Craft Dinner in transcript) at the band during performances, a unique fan interaction linked to an unnamed song. The practice is noted for the potential danger of the sharp box corners. "And to this day, fans insist on throwing boxes of craft dinner at the band as the result of this song."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

"That was the first ever indie release to be certified platinum in the history of Canadian music."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Founding Members and Humor
podcast.body: The group was founded by Ed Robertson and Steven Page, who channeled their distinctive sense of humor into their songwriting. "The group was formed by Ed Robertson and Stephen Page. They both had an odd sense of humor which they channeled into writing songs."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Given New Lease on Life by Network
podcast.body: Network Records is credited with providing the Barenaked Ladies with a new lease on life, suggesting a significant boost or turning point in their career. "And Network was responsible for giving the bare naked ladies a new lease on life."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The History of Indie Rock: Part 3

podcast.title: Indie Success and DIY Path
podcast.body: Similar to Lowest of the Low, the Barenaked Ladies achieved success as an indie band by committing to a "complete do-it-yourself path," demonstrating that major label backing was not always necessary for recognition in the early 90s Canadian scene. They frequently interacted with Lowest of the Low, highlighting a shared independent journey. "just like fellow Indies, the bare-naked ladies, a band who crossed paths with lowest of low, quite a bit, they decided to hell with everything."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Unique Humor and Songwriting
podcast.body: Founding members Ed Robertson and Steven Page shared an "odd sense of humor," which they effectively channeled into their songwriting, forming the core of the band's distinctive style and contributing to their nerdy image. "They both had an odd sense of humor, which they channeled into writing songs."

xref.title: Moe Berg in Supergroup The High Women
xref.body: Moe Berg is a member of "The High Women," an on-again, off-again Canadian indie supergroup that also includes Chris Murphy of Sloan, Craig Northe of Odds, and Steven Page, formerly of Barenaked Ladies. "He's also part of an on-again, off-again Canadian indie supergroup called The High Women, with Chris Murphy of Sloan, Craig Northe of Odds, and Steve Page, ex of the Bearnick and Ladies."

xref.title: Musician Friends' Benefit Concerts
xref.body: John Mann's musician friends, including members of the Barenaked Ladies, Blue Rodeo, and Sarah McLachlan, regularly organized benefit concerts to help fund his medical treatments. These events often featured collective performances of Spirit of the West classics. "And whenever one of these benefits was held, everybody joins in on this Spirit of the West class."
